A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same BGPS research. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and can be matched despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: V2 reports original prompt-search experiments, demographic frequencies, perplexities, generated images, linguistic analyses, and parameter ablations.

after.justification: V3 retains original empirical results and adds diffusion-transformer evaluations, a debiasing fine-tuning experiment, runtime measurements, and prompt-diversity and quality evaluations.

M1.justification: The BGPS objective and beam-search algorithm remain unchanged. V3 adds a limited adaptation for Flux and SD 3.5: classifiers use middle-transformer activations averaged over image tokens, excluding text tokens, instead of UNet mid-block features (Appendices A.1 and C.5).

E1.justification: V3 adds an actual downstream mitigation-training task: BGPS prompts are used to further fine-tune a debiased model (Appendix A.3). Occupational and non-occupational scenarios, gender/race/age targets, and multiple-person evaluation are retained. Changes to the tested diffusion models and LLMs concern model configurations rather than new demographic or domain coverage.

E2.justification: The main prompt-search comparators remain curated prompts, LLM-only, LLM (biased), and PEZ; Manually curated becomes Human-curated. V3 Table 8 additionally compares BGPS-prompt fine-tuning against occupation-prompt-only FT, giving FT a comparison role beyond its existing role as an audited model.

E3.justification: V2 describes filtering gender-revealing prompts as optional; v3 Section 4.1 states that attribute-revealing prompts are removed before evaluation using LLM assistance. V3 also replaces Qwen/Llama and DeepFloyd IF configurations with Flux/SD 3.5 evaluations using K=1, extends the SD 2.1 lambda sweep, adds a 2,000-step fine-tuning study, and introduces diversity and GPT-5 quality metrics. These substantially revise the reported evaluation design.

E4.justification: V3 adds analyses testing prompt diversity, fluency, coherence, plausibility, computational cost, and whether discovered prompts improve debiasing (Appendices A.3, B, and D.4). The cross-LLM sensitivity analysis is removed. The lambda, K, and timestep ablations already existed in v2; their reorganization should not be counted as entirely new analyses.

E5.justification: Main results retain 95% confidence intervals, and the K ablation retains uncertainty through plotted error bars. However, v2 Tables 15–16 provide uncertainty for timestep-ablation results, whereas v3 retains only the corresponding plot without error bars. Neither version reports independent-run counts or seeds.

E6.justification: Many retained results change: in Table 1, Mistral male-target BGPS at lambda=100 changes from 0.79 to 0.76 on FT, while LLM (biased) changes from 0.67 to 0.85 on Base. These are revised results under a changed reported filtering protocol, not demonstrated same-setting performance changes. V3 adds DiT, fine-tuning, runtime, and prompt-quality results, removes Qwen/Llama and DeepFloyd results, and drops timestep-specific female-perplexity entries. Occupation-conditioned, multiple-person, and age tables retain their results.

T1.justification: V3 Appendix B adds a computational-cost argument giving K×B×E×L UNet evaluations per prompt and claiming independence from T' through one-time initial denoising. The probability objective and existing mathematical reasoning otherwise remain stable; changing initial-noise notation from x0 to xT is a consistency correction.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction broaden the stated empirical applicability to newer diffusion models, including Flux, and add a claim about retaining prompt diversity beyond v2's perplexity-based interpretability emphasis. The central contribution of interpretable automatic bias discovery and the claim that debiased models retain vulnerabilities remain unchanged.

C2.justification: V3 substantially expands interpretation of aggregate demographic balance, explaining cancellation of opposing occupational biases, bias inherited from LLM prompts, and possible Difflens overcorrection. It interprets new fine-tuning results as evidence for useful hard examples and qualifies DiT results by their K=1 budget. The small-LLM instruction-following discussion disappears, while the original classifier-dependence limitations remain.

D1.justification: V3 newly documents H100 runtime, transformer feature pooling, explicit age and multiple-person instructions, and the additional fine-tuning duration. It removes access and configuration details for Qwen, Llama, and DeepFloyd IF. Most standard BGPS parameters, classifier sources, and evaluation-processing details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V3 removes the Qwen3 technical report, KCIF, and IHEval citations alongside the cross-LLM discussion. The positioning relative to visually guided decoding, prompt optimization, and bias mitigation remains largely unchanged. Several retained references receive publication metadata updates rather than representing newly cited work.

P1.justification: V3 extensively rewrites the quantitative-results narrative and reorganizes the appendices into additional experiments, efficiency, implementation, ablations, and qualitative results. Female and race results move into the main discussion, instructions and PEZ explanations are reorganized, and an Impact Statement is added. Much of the method and qualitative-analysis prose remains recognizable.

P2.justification: The main text changes from a single-column layout to a two-column conference format. Gender and race tables are merged and relocated, the bias histogram is combined with the word analysis, word clouds become a separate figure, and K tables become a four-panel plot. New experimental tables are added, while timestep tables are removed. Existing qualitative images are retained.

improvement.justification: V3 makes the central claims more assessable through diversity and quality measurements beyond perplexity, preliminary mitigation evidence, and clearer interpretation of baseline demographic balance. These provide a limited net gain despite removing the LLM-prior analysis and timestep uncertainty. Reporting inconsistencies constrain the improvement: Table 1 still gives PEZ female-bias scores where its stated filtering rule removes 100% of prompts.
